items.briefing:
Australians should be alert to a growing phishing trick where scammers send calendar invites containing malicious .ics files. These can appear as legitimate meeting requests but are designed to steal credentials or install malware — be cautious about accepting unexpected calendar invitations, especially from unknown senders. Separately, Scamwatch continues to report active scam campaigns targeting Australians, so remain vigilant about unsolicited contact via phone, email, or text.

On the local industry front, Australian firms DXC and Primary have launched a new AI-driven Zero Trust security service, reflecting growing investment in smarter cyber defences across the region.

**Practical tip:** Before accepting a calendar invite, verify the sender through a separate channel — don't click any links inside unexpected meeting requests.
